content: Sterol O-acyltransferase 1 (SOAT1), also referred to as acyl-Coenzyme A: cholesterol acyltransferase 1, is an enzyme encoded by the SOAT1 gene in humans. Acyl-coenzyme A: cholesterol acyltransferase (EC 2.3.1.26) is an intracellular protein that resides in the endoplasmic reticulum. Its primary function is to catalyze the formation of cholesterol esters from free cholesterol. This process is critical for the storage of cholesterol in cells. The accumulation of cholesterol esters in the form of cytoplasmic lipid droplets within macrophages and smooth muscle cells is a hallmark of the early stages of atherosclerotic plaque development. This phenomenon has been well-documented in studies, such as those by Cadigan et al. in 1988. An interactive pathway map related to this process, including genes, proteins, and metabolites, can be accessed and edited on WikiPathways under the Statin_Pathway_WP430 entry.
